newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Glaverbel buys rest of Czech Glavunion.
newsitem.headline: Glaverbel buys rest of Czech Glavunion.

text.p: Belgian glass maker Glaverbel SA said on Monday it had acquired the 27 percent of Czech glass maker Glavunion AS it did not already own, giving it 100 percent control over the company.
Glavunion said the deal cost it around 1.1 billion Belgian francs.

Glaverbel first entered Glavunion's capital in March 1991 as part of a government privatization. It initially acquired a 40 percent stake but had progressively increased that to 73 percent by July 1994.

Glaverbel bought the remaining 27 percent from Czech holding company Sklo Union AS. Sklo sold its interest following its merger in June with its shareholders, Czech investment company Harvard Industrial Holding and Bahama's Stratton Investments.
Glaverbel said, confirming previous statements, that it would pay for the investment from cash generated by a share swap with its parent Asahi Glass Co. Ltd. of Japan.
Glaverbel said also it had restarted production at one of Glavunion's two float glass lines after increasing the line's capacity to 600 tonnes from 310 tonnes a day.
The line had been shut since February.

"This boost to the plant's performance will further strengthen the profitability of Glavunion's activities and reinforces its position as leader in the market for flat glass in central Europe," Glaverbel said.
